title: First jobs: Luckey Roberts, Joe Jordan, Leroy Smith, Sissle
summary: He lists his first New York work, including parties with Luckey Roberts, a Broadway show, and Leroy Smith, before Noble Sissle; the interviewer asks about Roberts' Latin material.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I begin to get acquainted with those guys. So I remember very -- my first job. A fellow, old man those days, used to be a very popular ragtime piano player called Luckey Roberts. He used to (inaudible), he used to play those swanky private parties for the rich people.

And then was another guy too, very popular those days, a big man, they called him Joe Jordan. He was a big conductor, writer. So he took me to play one Broadway show called "Fast and Furious." The show didn't last much time. But that was a different idea.
And then I started playing with Leroy Smith. He was a violin player from Philadelphia; violin player, very popular those days. (Inaudible). So from there I went to Noble Sissle orchestra.
That was around late '31. I'm in late '31 already.

Let me ask -- let me interject while I think of it, did -- did Luckey Roberts ever play anything with a Latin tinge to it, because back in 1914-15 he wrote a couple of very fine ragtime tangoes, and in 1939 he wrote the whole so called Spanish Suite.
Yeah, he used to play something like that when I come to -- when I come to see --
This was a period when Rhumba was first coming in, right? With Catsee (phonetic) and -- Aspiazu
